solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: American working privately (2,6)

indicatorNotes.working: something working is in operation, set in motion, so the letters get moving

annotation.surface: An American employee who works behind closed doors.
annotation.walkthrough: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from press and public. 'American' looks like the usual A, but here all eight letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived legal phrase: a hearing held in a judge's private chambers rather than open court.

entries.clue: Element of riotous behaviour outlawed originally in prison (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally points to where each word starts, its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letters sit in the prison word

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison
first letters of Riotous Behaviour Outlawed, placed inside CAN

annotation.surface: A troublemaking inmate is part of the riot in a jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Element of riotous behaviour' reads as one phrase, but 'Element' alone is the definition: a chemical element.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: this is chemical element number 6, the basis of organic life.

entries.clue: Help — old boy needs raincoat when going up country (8)

indicatorNotes.going up: in a down clue, going up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

annotation.surface: An old man needs his raincoat for a trip up country.
annotation.walkthrough: AID + OB + MAC is written down and then read upwards as the whole answer. 'Up country' sounds like a journey inland, but 'country' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the answer is a South-East Asian nation, capital Phnom Penh.

entries.clue: Deep fish (4)

blocks.note: describing a low voice or note

annotation.surface: A fish that lives in deep water.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as a deep-sea fish, but each is a separate definition of BASS: one rhymes with 'face', the other with 'mass'.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the lowest singing voice, deep in pitch; the other is a spiny-finned fish.

entries.clue: Small animal cuddles her innocent child (6)

indicatorNotes.cuddles: to cuddle is to wrap your arms round, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal
taken as written, placed inside CUB

annotation.surface: A mother cuddling a small pet or her baby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Her' looks like part of the picture, the one doing the cuddling, but it is simply the letters HER being held.
annotation.definitionFit: Extended sense: from the winged infant angels of art, applied to a sweet, angelic-looking child.

entries.clue: Pay for the use of hotel on island retreat, shunning freebie? (4)

indicatorNotes.shunning: to shun is to avoid, so the word TREAT is kept out of 'retreat'

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
retreat minus TREAT (a freebie) leaves RE

annotation.surface: Renting a hotel for an island getaway, no complimentary extras.
annotation.walkthrough: A treat is something given free, so removing it from RETREAT leaves RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in verb form: renting a car or a hall means paying to use it for a time.

entries.clue: Fragment of coin case, one from ancient Peru (4)

indicatorNotes.Fragment of: a fragment is a piece broken off, so the answer is a piece of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

annotation.surface: An archaeologist finds a piece of a coin holder from ancient Peru.
annotation.walkthrough: The Inca ruled an empire in the Andes centred on Peru before the Spanish conquest.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a member of the Andean people whose empire the Spanish conquered in the 1530s.

entries.clue: Maybe scorpion found in handcar, I suspect (8)

indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not in its proper state, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone thinks a scorpion has crept into a railway handcar.
annotation.walkthrough: A handcar is a small hand-pumped railway trolley. 'Maybe' signals that a scorpion is only one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: scorpions belong to the eight-legged class that also includes spiders and mites.

entries.clue: Tree snake pulled back, grabbed by short infant (6)

indicatorNotes.pulled back: pulled back suggests drawn backwards, so the word is reversed
indicatorNotes.grabbed by: what is grabbed is held inside the grabber
indicatorNotes.short: short means cut off, the last letter dropped

blocks.note: BABY without its last letter; AOB goes after the first B

annotation.surface: A snake yanked away from a small baby it had grabbed in a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The snake and infant make a jungle rescue scene, but 'Tree' stands apart as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: a huge African tree with a swollen, water-storing trunk.

entries.clue: Unopened letters scattered about thoroughfare (6)

indicatorNotes.Unopened: a letter not opened has lost its opening, the first letter
indicatorNotes.scattered about: scattered letters are thrown in every direction, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: Unread post blown all over the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unopened letters' paints unread mail, but it tells you to drop the L from LETTERS before rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thoroughfare is any public road through a town.

entries.clue: One churchman or another missing company (4)

indicatorNotes.missing: what is missing is left out

blocks.note: a deacon is another kind of churchman

annotation.surface: Two clergymen, one of whom has lost his firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another churchman: DEACON, which minus CO gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the senior clergyman who heads a cathedral chapter.

entries.clue: Disadvantage of defender pursuing 0-0? (8)

indicatorNotes.pursuing: one who pursues comes after, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: in football, a back is a defender

annotation.surface: A football pundit on the downside of a defender chasing a goalless result.
annotation.walkthrough: 0-0 is a football scoreline, a goalless draw.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a feature that counts against something, a downside.

entries.clue: Civic dignitaries somehow learned to hold mass (8)

indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters come out in some other order
indicatorNotes.to hold: what is held sits inside the holder

blocks.note: m = mass in physics, held within the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Town worthies who have somehow picked up how to attend church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service; it is only M.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: senior members of an English borough or city council, now largely ceremonial.

entries.clue: Film-projection method Armenia developed under Communism, initially (8)

indicatorNotes.developed: something developed has changed form, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, what is under comes below, after the other piece
indicatorNotes.initially: initially points to the first letter

annotation.surface: A film technology Armenia built as a Soviet republic.
annotation.walkthrough: Armenia was part of the Soviet Union, which makes the surface plausible; 'developed' suggests film processing too.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade name: the 1950s widescreen system that threw three synchronised projector images onto a curved screen.

entries.clue: Conservative returned by electoral division (8)

blocks.note: to have returned is to be back
a ward is an electoral division of a town

annotation.surface: A Tory MP re-elected by his constituency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' and 'returned' paint a Tory winning a seat, but 'returned' just gives BACK and the definition is conservative in its lower-case sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A looser synonym: looking to the past and resisting progress, as a conservative outlook does.

entries.clue: Guardian, mostly enthusiastic, goes on through (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

annotation.surface: An eager caretaker who keeps talking right through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' might suggest the newspaper, but it is simply a person who looks after something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone in charge of looking after a place, animals or things.

entries.clue: Scandinavian also cycling east (4)

indicatorNotes.cycling: cycling moves letters round, the last one going to the front

blocks.note: AND with its last letter moved to the front

annotation.surface: A Scandinavian who also goes on a bike ride eastwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests bikes, a fair picture for someone from bike-loving Copenhagen, but it means rotating the letters of AND.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a native of Denmark, one of the Scandinavian countries.

entries.clue: Abandon deeds learnt every so often (6)

indicatorNotes.every so often: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: Someone occasionally forgets the lessons their actions taught them.
annotation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter from the start of 'deeds learnt' spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in verb form: to leave someone or a post without intending to return.

entries.clue: Fresh chapter that’s shocking and racy at the end (6)

indicatorNotes.at the end: the letter at the end of the word

blocks.note: eek! is what you say when something is shocking

annotation.surface: A new chapter in a novel that turns scandalous and saucy in its closing pages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' reads as new, as in a fresh chapter, but here it means impudent.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: fresh can mean impertinent or forward, as in 'don't get fresh with me'.

entries.clue: Beneficiary in Scottish town mentioned (4)

indicatorNotes.mentioned: a word mentioned is said out loud, so the answer sounds like it

blocks.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

annotation.surface: Someone named as an heir in a will from a Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: Ayr is a seaside town in south-west Scotland; the H of the answer is silent, so the two sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person entitled to receive someone's property when they die.

entries.clue: Indeed — right time (4)

blocks.note: yea = indeed, an old word for yes

annotation.surface: Someone agreeing that the moment has come.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right time' reads as the proper moment, but 'right' belongs to the wordplay and 'time' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: twelve months is a period of time.

entries.clue: Alight outside centre in Azores holiday location (6)

indicatorNotes.outside: one word goes outside, around, the other
indicatorNotes.centre in: the centre of the word, its middle letters

blocks.note: to alight is to come to rest, as a bird does
the middle two letters of azORes, placed inside REST

annotation.surface: Getting off a plane at a holiday spot in the Azores.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alight' suggests getting off transport, which suits the holiday picture, but here it means settle, REST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a town or complex built for visitors on holiday, as at the seaside.

entries.clue: Stopping retail, possibly, live for free (8)

indicatorNotes.Stopping: to stop a gap is to fill it, so this word goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.possibly: possibly means in some possible arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist; it goes inside LIRATE

annotation.surface: Quitting the shop trade in order to live for nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For free' looks like a single phrase meaning at no cost; 'free' alone is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in verb form: to release someone from captivity or control.

entries.clue: Behind POTUS? Tense doesn’t come into it! (4)

indicatorNotes.doesn’t come into it: the letter is not included, so it is removed

blocks.note: POTUS = President of the United States, here Donald Trump
T = tense in grammar, removed from TRUMP

annotation.surface: A cheeky jibe at the President's backside, with grammar left out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind POTUS' reads as supporting the President; 'Behind' is the definition, a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: the backside, the hindquarters of a person or animal.
